recipes.title: Shrimp Scampi

ingredients.name: raw large shrimp, peeled and deveined
dry white cooking wine (or chicken broth)

steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add linguini and cook until al dente according to package directions, reserving 1/2 cup of pasta water before draining.
While pasta is cooking, heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add minced garlic and crushed red pepper flakes; sauté for 1 minute until fragrant but not browned.
Add raw shrimp and chopped tomatoes to the skillet, cooking for 2 to 3 minutes until shrimp turn pink and opaque.
Pour in the dry white cooking wine (or chicken broth), season with salt and black pepper, and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes to reduce slightly.
Toss the drained linguini and chopped parsley directly into the skillet with the sauce, adding a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to coat the noodles smoothly.
recipes.swaps: Chicken broth can replace white wine; gluten-free pasta or zucchini noodles can replace linguini.
recipes.notes: Equipment: Large pasta pot, colander, large sauté pan. Quick-cooking dinner ready in under 30 minutes.

recipes.title: Garlic Prawns (Shrimp)

ingredients.name: raw large shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined, tail-on
garlic, finely chopped with a knife
dry white wine (Chardonnay or Pinot Grigio)

steps: Pat shrimp thoroughly dry with paper towels to ensure a crisp sear.
Toss shrimp in a bowl with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and black pepper. Let rest 10 to 15 minutes.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Add half of the shrimp in a single layer without crowding; sear undisturbed for 45 seconds per side until golden pink, then transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining tablespoon of olive oil to the skillet and sear the second batch of shrimp for 45 seconds per side.
Return the first batch of shrimp to the skillet, scatter in the chopped garlic, and stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the white wine; it will steam and sizzle vigorously. Simmer for 30 seconds while scraping up browned bits until the wine mostly evaporates.
Scatter the butter cubes and drizzle lemon juice into the pan. Swirl the skillet until the butter melts into an emulsified sauce, then toss through the fresh parsley.
Immediately transfer shrimp and garlic butter sauce to a warm serving platter and serve with crusty bread or over rice.

recipes.swaps: Low-sodium chicken broth can replace white wine; cilantro can substitute for parsley.
recipes.notes: Equipment: Large skillet, tongs. Do not use a garlic press as minced garlic will burn at high heat; chop with a knife.
